newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to set Luz del Sur share sale price today.
newsitem.headline: Peru to set Luz del Sur share sale price today.

text.p: The Peruvian government will set later Tuesday the sale price of its shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur, privatization officials said.

Brokers at the Lima Stock Exchange said the price would depend on the government's perception of international demand, but they expected it to be lower than the stock's opening trading level Tuesday of 3.45 soles.
"It all depends on what is happening abroad," said Hernando Pastor of T&J brokerage.
"We estimate that the shares will be fixed between 3.40 soles and 3.45 soles. 3.40 soles would be a good price (for investors)," said Victor Heredia of Fortuna brokerage.
Officials were due to announce the price after the close of the Lima market at 1700 local time/1700 EST.
The government is planning to place its entire 30 percent stake in Luz del Sur, representing 148.4 million shares, in a global offer intended to raise -- at home and abroad -- around $200 million.

President Alberto Fujimori has said the sale to individual Peruvian investors through the government's Citizens' Participation in Privatization Program has drawn offers from individual Peruvian investors worth 600 million soles ($233 million).
However, only 55 percent of the total shares on offer will go to this program, meaning unsatisfied demand is inevitable.
Officials have given no details on the level of demand from local or foreign institutional investors, who are expected to buy the remaining 45 percent of shares.
The Luz del Sur sale is Peru's most important share placement since July's successful $1.25 billion placement of a 26.6 percent state-owned share in telecommunications company Telefnica del Per.
The government has said it will define the distribution of the Luz del Sur shares it sells on December 13.

The former state-run electricity company was privatized in June 1994. A consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc bought a 60 percent stake for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston, chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale, have said they expected the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals, local bank Banco Continental directed a group of local banks that includes Banco de Crdito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander was selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru, Santander SAB, is directing a group of local brokerages to book-build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.
